messages:
Sam: Heads-up — noticed a token-level latency regression on dedicated pool gpu-pool-eu1 after the kernel-selector tweak deployed yesterday. 95th token latency jumped ~30ms. Logs + quick profile below.

Lucy: ugh, can you paste the profile + the pool id / route? :eyes:

Sam: pool=gpu-pool-eu1, route=/v1/generate/chat, recent run IDs attached. Quick perf snippet from perf trace (sampled):

```
# top hotspots (ms per token)
attention_kv_fast_kernel    0.8 ms
attention_kv_generic_fallback  35.2 ms  <-- large regression after selector
embedding_matmul             1.1 ms
kv_cache_lookup              0.5 ms
scheduler_batch_overhead     2.3 ms
```

Also seeing smaller effective batches for this route (avg batch_size=1.6 for seq<=128), but GPU utilization low (avg 34%). KV cache hit-rate dropped from 94% -> 78% for that pool on the last hour.

Raj: this smells like kernel selection choosing the generic path for short sequences when it should pick the flashed kernel. Could be heuristics tuned by sequence-length distribution. Also kv cache miss spike could be increasing cold-start token work. Can we get token-level latency breakdown in Grafana per-route? That will help split kernel vs batching vs kv cache.

Maria: Agreed. Minimal dashboard asks: per-route token P50/P95/P99, per-token-stage breakdown (kernel exec, kv lookup, scheduling wait), per-pool KPIs (gpu_util, queue_wait_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate), and a noisy-neighbor panel (stddev of tail latency across instances).

Kevin: I'll propose PromQL panels we can reuse. Example token-level histogram (Prometheus histogram of token latency):

```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
```

Per-route tokens/sec and average batch size:
```
sum(rate(tokens_processed_total{route=~"/v1/generate.*"}[1m])) by (route)
avg_over_time(batcher_batch_size{route="/v1/generate/chat"}[5m])
```

Jordan: For per-pool noisy neighbor detection: compare per-instance 95th latency and GPU active SM %, alert when per-pool stddev(95th_latency) > 15ms and mean_gpu_util < 45% while queue_wait_ms > 20ms. Also check host-level CPU steal.

infra-bot: deploybot: rollout redwood/runtime-selector v2.9 -> production (gpu-pool-eu1) started at 2025-06-01T10:05:00Z :rocket:

Sam: that deploybot line is the rollout that likely triggered this. Jordan — can you own updating the eng-runtime dashboard with these panels? Raj + Lucy can help validate kernel-selection rules in a canary cluster.

Jordan: I can do it. Will add panels and a small playbook for oncall (how to check kernel histograms and force fallback toggle). Linking ticket INF-472 and I'll attach dashboard JSON when done.

Lucy: I'll run a targeted canary with synthetic traffic (seqs 8/32/128/512) and toggle the selector flags. Let's compare token histograms pre/post. Will post results here.

Kevin: one more quick tip — add a KV cache hit-rate heatmap by key prefix to catch bad cache TTLs or key churn. We saw similar when client-side cache keys changed.

Maria: thanks all. Action items: Jordan -> dashboard + alert rules (INF-472), Lucy/Raj -> canary + kernel selector test, Sam -> attach representative traces. Ping @oncall if the alert fires. :thumbsup:

Sam: attaching two short traces and an example request id: r-6a7f3. I'll follow up with SLO impact calc tomorrow.

Jordan: noted, starting dashboard edits now. Will post panel snapshots when ready.
